source.title: MemoHarness: Agent Harnesses That Learn from Experience

new_findings.mechanism: Decompose the agent harness into six editable control dimensions (context, tools, generation, orchestration, memory, output); store both per-case diagnoses and distilled cross-case patterns; retrieve only a bounded evidence slice; adapt the harness per test case without test-time labels or a new search loop.
quantitative_evidence: Final selected harness improved over base on all three reported source benchmarks: Terminal-Bench 0.722->0.806, LiveCodeBench 0.900->0.967, FinanceAgent 0.600->0.767.
Cross-model transfer on Terminal-Bench improved every one of six additional tested models; mean gain +0.098, ranging from +0.038 on GPT-4.1 to +0.233 on GLM-5.

Cross-dataset transfer was selective rather than universal: the Terminal-Bench-derived harness improved MMMLU +0.030, StrongReject +0.030, SWE-Bench Pro +0.059, while saturated suites did not move and LawBench results were mixed.

On the 18-task Terminal-Bench held-out split, MemoHarness used 14.18M input tokens but 13.32M were cached; reported cost $6.89 versus Codex $10.28 and Claude Code $9.51 under the paper's cost accounting, with the caching assumption explicitly material.

Operation-level adjacent-transition analysis found some newly added inspection/condition-check operations strongly associated with reward increases (e.g. cat positive-transition rate 72.7%, +59.5 pp over a ~13.2% baseline), while curl/echo/grep were weak or negative. Authors present these as associations, not causal ablations.
new_findings.evidence_scope: The paper is recent and reproducible, but explicitly says larger studies and finer component attribution are needed. Product-specific baseline comparisons are not pure scaffold ablations. Cross-dataset gains are selective. Operation-level associations are not randomized causal effects.
new_findings.o_relevance: Very close to O's Context Kernel problem. It supports optimizing the entire control layer as structured dimensions, retaining success and failure diagnoses, distilling global patterns, and retrieving bounded case-relevant slices rather than accumulating full history. It also supplies a direct transfer test: a useful O improvement should survive at least some held-out tasks/models rather than only its search benchmark.

source.title: Group-Evolving Agents: Open-Ended Self-Improvement via Experience Sharing

new_findings.mechanism: Treat a group, not an isolated lineage, as the evolutionary unit; pool experiences from multiple branches so discoveries can be consolidated rather than dying in branch isolation.
quantitative_evidence: Under the reported matched evolved-agent budget, GEA reached 71.0% versus DGM 56.7% on SWE-bench Verified and 88.3% versus 68.3% on Polyglot.
The paper reports framework-level bug repair in 1.4 iterations on average versus 5 for the compared self-evolving method.
Analysis reports the best GEA agent integrated 8 of 9 key functionalities, versus 5 for the best DGM agent; the best GEA agent incorporated experience from 17 unique ancestors versus 9 for DGM.
new_findings.evidence_scope: Coding-agent domain and a specific DGM-derived evolutionary substrate. The headline comparison tests a composite group-evolution method rather than independently randomizing every element of experience sharing, group selection, and consolidation. Treat as strong candidate evidence, not universal proof.
new_findings.o_relevance: Directly strengthens the archive lesson from DGM: diversity is not enough if branches cannot exchange useful discoveries. For O, compare isolated candidate lineages against a shared-evidence population where lessons/patches can transfer across branches, while preserving provenance so harmful transfer can be traced.

source.title: Scaling Self-Evolving Agents via Parametric Memory

new_findings.mechanism: At context/memory boundaries, distill grounded QA supervision and write it into fast LoRA weights during the same episode, so experience changes the policy rather than only occupying prompt space. Initialize the fast-weight subspace with pretrained-weight SVD and freeze that subspace while updating coefficients.
quantitative_evidence: Before RL, on LongMemEval-S TMEM beat the strongest explicit-memory baseline by +4.79 F1/+2.34 EM with Qwen3-4B and +10.21 F1/+7.02 EM with Qwen3-8B.

On multi-objective search with Qwen3-4B it beat the strongest explicit-memory baseline by +1.92 F1/+1.13 EM (4 objectives) and +1.86/+1.16 (8 objectives); one Qwen3-8B 4-objective gain was only +1.00 F1/+0.23 EM and the authors call that case directional rather than decisive.

After matched RL, TMEM received larger absolute gains than explicit-memory methods: +5.12 F1/+5.02 EM on LoCoMo and +4.92/+4.84 on LongMemEval-S; on search it exceeded the strongest explicit-memory baseline after RL by +4.34 F1/+3.29 EM (4 objectives) and +4.36/+2.63 (8 objectives).
SVD initialization ablation on Qwen3-4B improved LoCoMo from 24.26/12.15 F1/EM to 25.72/15.40 and LongMemEval-S from 38.54/22.33 to 41.24/25.54.
Supervision-form ablation was large: on LongMemEval-S raw next-token 10.37/7.62 F1/EM, free-form summary 35.44/20.18, grounded QA pairs 41.24/25.54.
Freezing the SVD projection subspace lost only 0.27 F1/0.12 EM on LongMemEval-S versus training both LoRA factors, reducing online update work with nearly unchanged accuracy.

Context-trigger budget had a bell-shaped optimum: too-frequent compression discarded detail, while overly large working context degraded extraction quality; best reported Lmax differed by dataset (4096 LoCoMo, 12288 LongMemEval-S).
new_findings.evidence_scope: Preprint, small Qwen3-4B/8B backbones, memory-centric benchmarks, filtered CL-Bench uses an answerable subset, and online parameter updates add compute/GPU cost. This is not evidence that O should immediately modify its foundation-model weights. It is evidence for a testable fast-memory mechanism under matched conditions.
new_findings.o_relevance: This is a genuine context asymmetry for O: current O design emphasizes selective external context, whereas TMEM asks whether some durable high-value experience should be moved out of prompt/context and into a bounded fast-adaptation substrate. A safe first test would be a small adapter/proxy model or task-local learner, not modification of the primary model.

updated_evidence_judgments: The strongest recurring pattern across AI4AI-Bench, MemoHarness, GEA, GEPA, MARS and TMEM is not generic 'self-reflection'. It is structured credit assignment plus preservation/reuse of diagnostic information: identify the intervention layer, retain failure/success evidence, keep multiple viable branches, and make information transferable to later decisions.

Several results explicitly show non-monotonicity or scope limits: PAST-Bench component interactions reverse by capability; MemoHarness transfer is selective; TMEM has small directional gains in at least one setting; AI4AI's learning-side advantage is observational. O should therefore test mechanism-level claims under matched controls rather than importing whole systems.
